plain.li: [ch:head,theirs,w:industrial,!empire] The {TOWN} Courier\nPrinted when there is news, and sometimes when there is not.
[ch:head,theirs,w:industrial,!empire] The {TOWN} Weekly Sheet\nOne page. Read it twice.
[ch:head,theirs,w:industrial|w:spacer,!empire] News from {TOWN}\nAs set down by whoever had the pen this week.
[ch:head,theirs,w:spacer,!empire] {TOWN} Information Bulletin\nCycle summary. Distribution: all residents, and one friend.
[ch:head,theirs,w:spacer,!empire] {TOWN} Local Feed, printed copy\nFor those without a terminal, or without the patience for one.
[ch:head,theirs,empire] The Gazette of {TOWN}\nIssued by leave of the court. Matters of standing first.
[ch:head,theirs,w:tribal] The season at {TOWN}, as it was told.
[ch:head,theirs,w:tribal] What the people of {TOWN} saw this season, told at the fire.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor,!w:tribal] TIMES HARD. Since {FORTUNEWHY}, the town has been struggling, and the council asks everyone to mend before they buy.

[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor,!w:tribal] HARD TIMES CONTINUE. Stores are low and spirits lower. The sheet reminds readers that it has been worse, and that it was not much fun then either.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing,!w:tribal] TRADE IS UP. More wagons on the road than anyone can remember, and the inn has run out of beds and started renting out the stable.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing,!w:tribal] GOOD TIMES. Since {FORTUNEWHY}, the town has done well. Readers are asked not to boast about it on the road; it attracts the wrong sort.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor,w:tribal] This was a lean season. The meat-racks were thin and the old ones ate last.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing,w:tribal] This was a fat season. The children grew round and the dogs grew lazy.
[ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation:bad,!w:tribal] STILL WITH US: {TOWNSITUATION}. The sheet will say no more about it, as everybody is tired of hearing about it, the sheet included.
[ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation:good,!w:tribal] GOOD NEWS: {TOWNSITUATION}, and long may it last.
[ch:item,chs:situation,situation,!w:tribal] FROM FURTHER OFF: there is talk on every road of {SITUATION}, and travellers bring a new rumour of it every day, most of them wrong.
[ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation,w:tribal] This was the season of {TOWNSITUATION}. The old ones say it will be remembered.
[ch:item,chs:loss,!w:tribal] IN MEMORY. {LOST}, {LOSTTITLE}, has died. The town turned out for the burial, and many stayed late, telling stories that {LOST} would have disputed.
[ch:item,chs:loss,w:tribal] {LOST} went into the dark this season. We sang the long song for them, all of it.
[ch:item,chs:head,town:newhead,!w:tribal] NEW AT THE HEAD OF THINGS: {HEAD}, our new {HEADTITLE}, who has promised nothing, which the sheet considers a good start.
[ch:item,chs:head,town:headdied] {OLDHEAD} is gone, and {HEAD} leads now. The town wishes {HEAD} well, and patience.
[ch:item,chs:head,town:head,!town:newhead,!w:tribal] {HEAD}, our {HEADTITLE}, reports that all is well, and asks that anyone who disagrees take it up in person, soon, and briefly.
[ch:item,chs:head,town:newhead,w:tribal] {HEAD} speaks for the people now. The old ones gave over the staff, and nobody argued, which is not like us.
[ch:item,chs:ill,!w:tribal] ILLNESS. {ILL}, {ILLTITLE}, is unwell, and visitors are asked to bring soup, not opinions.
[ch:item,chs:ill,w:tribal] {ILL} is sick. The healers sit with them, and the drums are quiet.
[ch:item,chs:war,their:war,!w:tribal] THE WAR. There is still no peace with {WAR}. The road toward them is closed to anyone with sense.
[ch:item,chs:war,their:war,war:winning,!w:tribal] THE WAR goes well, they say, though nobody who says so has been near it.
[ch:item,chs:war,their:war,war:losing,!w:tribal] THE WAR goes badly. Readers are asked to keep their opinions to themselves and their doors bolted.
[ch:item,chs:war,their:war,w:tribal] The people are still at war with {WAR}. The young hunters paint their faces every evening, and the old ones shake their heads.
[ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace,!w:tribal] PEACE. The war with {PEACEWITH} is over. The sheet hopes this one lasts longer than the last.
[ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace,w:tribal] We have made peace with {PEACEWITH}. The spears are back on the wall, where they look better.

[ch:item,chs:newtown,region:newtown,!w:tribal] NEIGHBOURS. A new town, {NEWTOWN}, has gone up within reach, settled by {NEWTOWNPEOPLE}. Nobody knows anything about them yet, which has not stopped anyone talking.
[ch:item,chs:newtown,region:newtown,w:tribal] New people have made a place, {NEWTOWN}, people of {NEWTOWNPEOPLE}. We will go and look at them when the season turns.
[ch:item,chs:camp,region:camp:theirfoe] TRAVEL. Word is that a {RAIDCAMP} stands near {COLONY}. Anyone going that way is advised to go in numbers.
[ch:item,chs:caravan,town:caravan] TRADE. A caravan is setting out for {COLONY}. Anyone with letters or small parcels for that way should bring them to the gate before it leaves.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:held,!rd:road,theirs] THE RAID. Raiders came at the town and were beaten off. The sheet thanks everyone who was on the wall, and everyone who brought them soup.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:hurt|rd:end:sacked,theirs] THE RAID. The town was hit hard. Those with room are asked to take in those without. Those with grain are asked the same.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:ongoing,theirs] RAIDERS still about. The gate closes at dusk, and anyone outside after that will be left there to think about it.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:road,theirs] THE ROAD. Wagons have been set upon. Travel in company, and not at dusk.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:helped,theirs] THANKS to the people of {COLONY}, who stood on our walls when it mattered. The sheet will not forget, and neither will the town.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:unknown,!rd:you,theirs] FIGHTING at the town. The sheet will print the whole of it when the whole of it is known.
[ch:item,chs:deed,deed:good] ABOUT OUR NEIGHBOURS. The town still talks of how the people of {COLONY} {DEED}. The sheet sets it down here so it is not forgotten.
[ch:item,chs:colony,colony:known] HEARD ON THE ROAD: {COLONY} is known for {KNOWNFOR} these days. The sheet has no opinion, except that it is nice to be known for something.
[ch:item,chs:short,town:short:food] SHORTAGES. Food is tight. Anyone with a garden is asked to grow more than they need, and anyone with more than they need is asked to say so.
[ch:item,chs:short,town:short:medicine] SHORTAGES. No medicine to be had. The herb-gatherers are out dawn to dusk and could use a hand, and a cup of something warm.
[ch:item,chs:short,town:short:fuel] SHORTAGES. Fuel is short. Burn sparingly, sleep close.
[ch:item,chs:short,town:short:hands] SHORTAGES. Not enough hands for the work. Anyone who can hold a tool is wanted in the fields.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:spring,!w:tribal] THE WEATHER. Mud. More mud expected. The sheet regrets it.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:summer,!w:tribal] THE WEATHER. Hot. The well is low and tempers are short, and the sheet asks everyone to share the shade.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:autumn,!w:tribal] THE WEATHER. The leaves are down and the stores are up. Wrap up warm and look to your roof.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:winter,!w:tribal] THE WEATHER. Snow. Look in on your neighbours, especially the old ones, especially the ones who say they are fine.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:winter,home:frozen,!w:tribal] THE WEATHER. Cold, as ever. The sheet is printed indoors, by the fire, and apologises for the soot.
[ch:item,chs:season,home:desert,!w:tribal] THE WEATHER. Dry. Not a drop since anyone can remember. The sheet is written in the shade, and slowly.
[ch:item,chs:season,w:tribal] The {ANIMALS} came down from the hills early this season. The old ones say that means a long cold.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:summer,w:tribal] The sun sat on us all season like a fat dog. We slept in the day and hunted at night.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] LOST: one brown goat, answers to nothing. If found, keep it; it is yours now.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] FOUND: a boot, left, size large, in the well. The owner may collect it, and explain.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] FOR SALE: a cart, one wheel missing. Or a wheel, one cart missing. Enquire at the smithy.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] WANTED: someone who can play the fiddle. Someone who thinks they can need not apply.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] NOTICE: the bridge is closed again. It is the same bridge. It is the same reason.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] THANKS to whoever left the basket of eggs at the widow's door. She knows it was you.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] REMINDER: the well is for water. It is not for cooling drinks, washing dogs, or settling arguments.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] APOLOGY: the sheet regrets an error in its last issue. The pig did not win the vote. The pig was not standing.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] LOST: a hat, green, of sentimental value. If you are wearing it, you know who you are.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] FOR SWAP: one rooster, very loud, for one rooster, less loud.
[ch:notice,w:spacer] SYSTEM NOTICE: the water reclaimer will be down for maintenance. Residents are advised to drink responsibly and wash briefly.
[ch:notice,w:spacer] LOST: one cleaning drone, answers to its serial number, last seen heading for the fields with an air of purpose.
[ch:notice,w:industrial] NOTICE: the generator will be off on the third evening for repairs. Bring a candle and a good story.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] The dog with the white ear has had puppies. Anyone who wants one should ask the dog.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] Someone has been taking the good stones from the river. The river knows who.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] A child found a feather as long as an arm. Nobody knows what bird. The child sleeps with it.
[ch:end,theirs,!w:tribal,!empire] Printed at {TOWN}. Pass it on.
[ch:end,!w:tribal,!empire] The sheet will appear again when there is news, or paper, whichever comes first.
[ch:end,w:spacer,!empire] END OF BULLETIN.
[ch:end,w:tribal] That is the season. The fire is out.
[ch:end,empire] By order. Copies to be displayed in the square.
[olde,ch:head,theirs] Here beginneth the tidings of {TOWN}, as cried in the market by the town crier.
[olde,ch:head,theirs] The Roll of {TOWN}, wherein are set down the doings of the season.
[olde,ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor,theirs] Item: the times are hard at {TOWN}, and the council biddeth all to mend ere they buy.
[olde,ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing] Item: trade is brisk, and the inn hath no bed to spare.
[olde,ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation:bad] Item: {TOWNSITUATION} is with us yet, and none will speak more of it.
[olde,ch:item,chs:loss] Item: {LOST}, {LOSTTITLE}, is dead, and all the town went out to the burying.
[olde,ch:item,chs:head,town:newhead] Item: {HEAD} is made {HEADTITLE}, and hath promised naught, which is a good beginning.
[olde,ch:item,chs:ill] Item: {ILL}, {ILLTITLE}, lieth sick. Bring broth, not counsel.
[olde,ch:item,chs:war,their:war] Item: there is yet no peace with {WAR}, and the road toward them is shut to all of sense.
[olde,ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace] Item: peace is made with {PEACEWITH}, and may it outlast the last.
[olde,ch:item,chs:newtown,region:newtown] Item: a new town, {NEWTOWN}, is raised within reach, by {NEWTOWNPEOPLE}.
[olde,ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:held,!rd:road,theirs] Item: reavers came against the town and were beaten off, and all honour to them that kept the wall.
[olde,ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:hurt|rd:end:sacked,theirs] Item: the reavers did us great hurt. Them that have room are bidden take in them that have none.
[olde,ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:helped,theirs] Item: our thanks to the folk of {COLONY}, who stood upon our wall in the hour of need.
[olde,ch:item,chs:deed,deed:good] Item: the town speaketh yet of how the folk of {COLONY} {DEED}.
[olde,ch:item,chs:short,town:short:food] Item: food is scant. Them that have more than they need are bidden say so.
[olde,ch:item,chs:season,season:winter] Item: snow. Look to thy neighbours, and chiefly to the old.
[olde,ch:item,chs:season,season:summer] Item: great heat. The well is low and tempers are short.
[olde,ch:notice] Item: lost, a goat of the brown sort, that answereth to naught. Whosoever findeth it may keep it, and good luck to them.
[olde,ch:notice] Be it known: the bridge is shut again, for the selfsame cause as before.
[olde,ch:notice] Item: a fiddler is wanted for the feast. One that only thinketh he can play need not come.
[olde,ch:end] Thus endeth the roll. Heaven keep the town.
[sv:machine,ch:head,theirs] SETTLEMENT STATUS DIGEST: {TOWN}.\nFORMAT: ITEMISED.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor] ECONOMIC STATUS: DEPRESSED. CAUSE: {FORTUNEWHY}.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing] ECONOMIC STATUS: FAVOURABLE. RESIDENTS: SMUG.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:loss] PERSONNEL LOSS: {LOST}, {LOSTTITLE}. RECORDED WITH REGRET.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:war,their:war] HOSTILITIES WITH {WAR}: ONGOING.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,theirs] SECURITY INCIDENT: LOGGED. DETAILS ON REQUEST.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:season] WEATHER: WITHIN TOLERANCES.
[sv:machine,ch:notice] MAINTENANCE: SCHEDULED. RESIDENTS: UNCOOPERATIVE.
[sv:machine,ch:end] END OF DIGEST.
[sv:hive,ch:head,theirs] What the many of {TOWN} counted.
[sv:hive,ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor] The stores are thin. We are thinner. We share.
[sv:hive,ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing] The stores are full. We are many. We are glad.
[sv:hive,ch:item,chs:loss] {LOST} is gone. We are fewer by one. We feel it, all of us.
[sv:hive,ch:item,chs:season] The weather turned. We turned with it.
[sv:hive,ch:notice] The young have hatched. They are loud. We are proud.
[sv:hive,ch:end] That is the count. We have counted.
[olde,ch:head,theirs] Oyez, oyez, oyez: the crier's roll of {TOWN}, cried at the market cross and set down here for them that were not by.
[olde,ch:head,theirs] The tidings of {TOWN}, as the bellman cried them, word for word, save where he was drunk.

[olde,ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing,theirs] Item: the town prospereth since {FORTUNEWHY}, and the council biddeth all not to boast of it upon the road, lest it draw the wrong sort.
[olde,ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation:good] Item: {TOWNSITUATION} hath gone well for us, and thanks are given at every board.
[olde,ch:item,chs:loss] Item: the town mourneth {LOST}, {LOSTTITLE}, and the bell shall be rung each eve till the month's end.
[olde,ch:item,chs:head,town:headdied] Item: {OLDHEAD} being dead, {HEAD} is made {HEADTITLE} in that stead, and all are bidden to the oath at the cross.
[olde,ch:item,chs:ill] Item: prayers are asked for {ILL}, {ILLTITLE}, that lieth sick, and broth, which is likelier to help.
[olde,ch:item,chs:war,their:war,war:winning] Item: the war with {WAR} goeth well, and the reeve saith it shall be ended ere harvest, which he said last harvest also.
[olde,ch:item,chs:war,their:war,war:losing] Item: the war with {WAR} goeth ill, and all that can bear arms are bidden to the muster.
[olde,ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace] Item: there shall be no more fighting with {PEACEWITH}, by order, and any that striketh the first blow shall answer for it.
[olde,ch:item,chs:newtown,region:newtown] Item: strangers, {NEWTOWNPEOPLE}, have raised a town called {NEWTOWN}, and are said to keep a good market.
[olde,ch:item,chs:camp,region:camp:theirfoe,theirs] Item: there is word of a {RAIDCAMP} near {COLONY}, and our friends there are bidden keep their gate barred.
[olde,ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:ongoing,theirs] Item: reavers are about the town yet. None shall go out after dark, and the gate shall be shut at vespers.
[olde,ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:road,theirs] Item: wagons have been set on upon the high road. Go in company, and not at dusk.
[olde,ch:item,chs:deed,deed:good,theirs] Item: the council would have it remembered how the folk of {COLONY} {DEED}, and so it is cried here again.
[olde,ch:item,chs:colony,colony:known,theirs] Item: travellers say {COLONY} is known in these parts for {KNOWNFOR}. The crier hath no opinion on it, save that it is well to be known for somewhat.
[olde,ch:item,chs:caravan,town:caravan,theirs] Item: a caravan maketh ready for the road to {COLONY}. Them that would send aught, bring it to the reeve by week's end.
[olde,ch:item,chs:short,town:short:medicine] Item: physic is scant. The herb-wives go out at dawn and would be glad of a hand.
[olde,ch:item,chs:short,town:short:fuel] Item: wood is short. Burn sparing, sleep close.
[olde,ch:item,chs:short,town:short:hands] Item: hands are wanting in the fields. Any that can hold a sickle, come.
[olde,ch:item,chs:season,season:spring] Item: mud. More mud is looked for. The crier regretteth it.
[olde,ch:item,chs:season,season:autumn] Item: the leaves are down and the swine are in the wood. Look to thine acorns.
[olde,ch:notice] Be it known: the miller's dog hath bitten the miller again, and the miller asketh that none take the dog's part.
[olde,ch:notice] Item: a purse was found by the well. Whoso can say what is in it may have it. None hath yet said aright.
[olde,ch:notice] Wanted: one that can mend a bell and keep a secret. Ask at the chapel door, quietly.
[olde,ch:notice] Item: the ale at the Crossed Keys is found to be watered, and the alewife fined, and the ale is no better.
[olde,ch:notice] Let it be known that the old oak by the green is not to be climbed, by order, and that the children have read the order and climbed it.
[olde,ch:end] So endeth the crier's roll. Keep the peace, and keep thy gate barred.
[olde,ch:end] Thus much was cried. The rest was drowned out by the fishwives.
[ch:head,theirs,w:tribal] Here is what the people of {TOWN} told at the fire when the moon was round.
[ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation:bad,w:tribal] The people speak of {TOWNSITUATION}, and the old ones look at the sky more than they used to.
[ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation:good,w:tribal] It is said at the fire that {TOWNSITUATION} has been kind to us, and the old ones thank it in the evenings.
[ch:item,chs:loss,w:tribal] {LOST} has gone to the long fire. The people sang the whole night, and the song is longer now by one name.
[ch:item,chs:head,town:newhead,w:tribal] {HEAD} sits in the elder's place now, and the people are learning to wait for {HEAD} to speak first.
[ch:item,chs:ill,w:tribal] {ILL} lies sick, and the healer sings over the sickness every night, and the children are being very quiet.
[ch:item,chs:war,their:war,w:tribal] The war with {WAR} goes on. The young ones paint their faces before they eat.
[ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace,w:tribal] There is peace with {PEACEWITH}. The war drums have been put away in the dry place, and the dancing drums brought out.
[ch:item,chs:newtown,region:newtown,w:tribal] A new people, {NEWTOWNPEOPLE}, have made a camp at {NEWTOWN}. The hunters say they are noisy, but they share.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:held,!rd:road,theirs,w:tribal] Raiders came through the grass and were driven back. The dogs are very proud of themselves.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:hurt|rd:end:sacked,theirs,w:tribal] Raiders came and took from us. The people share what is left, and the meat-racks are thin.
[ch:item,chs:deed,deed:good,theirs,w:tribal] The people of {COLONY} {DEED}. We tell it at the fire so the young ones know who our friends are.
[ch:item,chs:colony,colony:known,theirs,w:tribal] Travellers say {COLONY} is known for {KNOWNFOR}. The old ones nodded, as if they had known already.
[ch:item,chs:caravan,town:caravan,theirs,w:tribal] Some of us are making ready to walk to {COLONY} with things to trade. If you want anything, tell the runner.
[ch:item,chs:short,town:short:food,w:tribal] The meat is short. The hunters go out every day and come back with less every day.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:winter,w:tribal] The snow came and stayed. We are close around the fires and the stories are long.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:spring,w:tribal] The geese came back and the ice went out of the river. The young ones swam on the first warm day and regretted it.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:summer,w:tribal] The berries are early and the flies are worse. Everyone is purple-handed and scratching.
[ch:item,chs:season,season:autumn,w:tribal] The herds are moving, and so are we. The old ones say the cold will come early. They say it every year. They are right half the time.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] Someone has taken the good scraping stone. Whoever it is, the grandmother knows, and she is waiting.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] Two of the young ones are courting. Everyone knows. They think nobody knows.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] The black dog has had pups. The black dog will not say who the father is.
[ch:end,w:tribal] That is what was told. The fire went low, and we went to sleep.
[ch:end,w:tribal] That is the season. The next one is already coming over the hill.
[ch:head,theirs,empire] The Court Circular of {TOWN}\nMatters of honour, title and precedence, set out in order.
[ch:head,theirs,empire] By Leave of the Throne: Notices of {TOWN}\nRead aloud in the hall at the third bell.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing,empire] PROSPERITY. The holding has done well since {FORTUNEWHY}, and the court is pleased to note it in the record.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor,empire] PRUDENCE. The holding is in straitened times since {FORTUNEWHY}. Households of rank are asked to set an example of restraint.
[ch:item,chs:loss,empire] MOURNING. The court records the death of {LOST}, {LOSTTITLE}. Mourning dress for one week; no music in the halls.
[ch:item,chs:head,town:newhead,empire] PRECEDENCE. {HEAD} is confirmed as {HEADTITLE} of the holding. All are reminded of the proper forms of address.
[ch:item,chs:war,their:war,empire] THE WAR. Operations against {WAR} continue. The court reminds all that the Empire does not discuss the details of its wars in gazettes.
[ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace,empire] PEACE. Terms are concluded with {PEACEWITH}. The banners will be lowered at sunset.
[ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation,empire] NOTICE OF EVENTS. The court is aware of {TOWNSITUATION}, and has the matter in hand.
[ch:item,chs:colony,colony:known,theirs,empire] OF OUR NEIGHBOURS. The holding of {COLONY} is spoken of at court for {KNOWNFOR}. The court takes note.
[ch:notice,empire] COURT DRESS. For the season, the darker blues. Gold thread at the cuff only. Anyone seen in green will be spoken to.
[ch:notice,empire] AUDIENCES. Petitions to the hall are heard on the first and fourth days. Petitioners will kneel where marked.
[ch:notice,empire] LOST. One signet, of no great value except to its owner, who is anxious. Returns to the steward. No questions will be asked, at first.
[ch:end,empire] Given under seal. Copies to the steward, the chapel and the gate.

[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:thriving|town:flourishing,w:spacer] ECONOMY: up. Since {FORTUNEWHY}, credit is flowing and the market stalls have extended their hours, to nobody's surprise but the stallholders'.
[ch:item,chs:fortune,town:struggling|town:poor,w:spacer] ECONOMY: down. Since {FORTUNEWHY}, rationing tier two is in effect. Questions to the quartermaster, complaints to the void.
[ch:item,chs:situation,town:situation:bad,w:spacer] ADVISORY: {TOWNSITUATION}. Stay indoors when the sirens sound. Stay calm when they do not.
[ch:item,chs:loss,w:spacer] OBITUARY: {LOST}, {LOSTTITLE}. Remembered at the evening watch. Personal messages to the family through the board.
[ch:item,chs:war,their:war,w:spacer] SECURITY: hostilities with {WAR} remain active. Report unfamiliar signals to the comms desk.
[ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace,w:spacer] SECURITY: the ceasefire with {PEACEWITH} holds. The perimeter guns have been told to relax. They have not been told how.
[ch:item,chs:raid,rd:now,rd:end:held,!rd:road,theirs,w:spacer] SECURITY: raid repelled at the perimeter. Thanks to the watch, and to the turrets, which do not read this.
[ch:item,chs:season,w:spacer] CLIMATE: within tolerances. The weather station would like to remind everyone that it is not personally responsible.
[ch:notice,w:spacer] LOST AND FOUND: one maintenance drone, answering to Biscuit. Last seen heading for the hydroponics bay with intent.
[ch:notice,w:spacer] REMINDER: the airlock is not a shortcut.
[ch:notice,w:spacer] SOCIAL: film night in the mess, third cycle. The same film as last time. There is only the one film.
[ch:notice,w:industrial] FOR SALE: one bicycle, nearly new, ridden only by a man who has since decided to walk.
[ch:notice,w:industrial] TO WHOEVER KEEPS MOVING THE BENCH OUTSIDE THE POST OFFICE: we know it is you.
[ch:notice,w:industrial] DANCE at the hall on the first evening of next week. The band has promised to learn a second tune.
[ch:item,chs:short,town:short:fuel,w:industrial] COAL. The supply is short and the price is long. Wear your coat indoors and think warm thoughts.
[ch:item,chs:caravan,town:caravan,theirs,!w:tribal] OUTWARD BOUND. A wagon train leaves for {COLONY} at the end of the month. Parcels to the depot by the twentieth.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace] HOSTILITIES WITH {PEACEWITH}: CONCLUDED. RESIDENTS: CAUTIOUSLY PLEASED.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:head,town:newhead] LEADERSHIP: CHANGED. NEW HEAD: {HEAD}. ADJUSTMENT PERIOD: ONGOING.
[sv:machine,ch:item,chs:ill] MEDICAL: {ILL} INCAPACITATED. PROGNOSIS: UNDER REVIEW.
[sv:hive,ch:item,chs:war,their:war] We are at war with {WAR}. The outer cells are full of the angry. We are angry together.
[sv:hive,ch:item,chs:ill] {ILL} is unwell. The many bring food to the still one.
[sv:hive,ch:item,chs:season,season:winter] Cold. We cluster. The centre is warm. We take turns at the edge.
[ch:item,chs:ill,!w:tribal] SICKNESS. {ILL}, {ILLTITLE}, is unwell. Visitors are asked to bring soup, and to leave quickly.
[ch:item,chs:peace,their:peace,!w:tribal] PEACE. Terms are settled with {PEACEWITH}. The sheet expects the peace to last, and will print a correction if it does not.
[ch:item,chs:newtown,region:newtown,!w:tribal] NEIGHBOURS. A new settlement, {NEWTOWN}, has been raised by {NEWTOWNPEOPLE}. The sheet has sent nobody to find out what they are like, but will.
[ch:item,chs:camp,region:camp:theirfoe,theirs,!w:tribal] A WARNING. There is word of a {RAIDCAMP} near {COLONY}. Travellers on that road should go in company.
[ch:item,chs:caravan,town:caravan,theirs,!w:tribal] THE CARAVAN. Our wagons leave for {COLONY} at the end of the month. Letters and parcels to the yard by the day before.
[ch:item,chs:deed,deed:good,theirs,!w:tribal] REMEMBERED. The town has not forgotten how the people of {COLONY} {DEED}. A vote of thanks was passed, unanimously, which is a first.
[ch:item,chs:colony,colony:known,theirs,!w:tribal] REPUTATIONS. {COLONY} is said on the road to be known for {KNOWNFOR}. The sheet passes this on without comment, except this one.
[ch:item,chs:head,town:headdied,!w:tribal] SUCCESSION. Following the death of {OLDHEAD}, {HEAD} takes up the office of {HEADTITLE}. The town wishes {HEAD} well, and patience.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] LOST: one glove, left. FOUND: one glove, right. The sheet has done what it can.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] The choir meets on the second evening of each week. New voices welcome. Good voices more welcome.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] To whoever has been leaving apples on the step of the schoolhouse: the teacher says thank you, and also that she knows.
[ch:notice,!w:tribal] The ferry will not run on market day, as the ferryman will be at market.
[ch:end,!w:tribal,!empire] That is the sheet. Pass it on when you have read it, and do not wrap fish in it until then.
[olde,ch:notice] Item: the bridge-toll is raised a farthing, and the bridge is no better for it.
[olde,ch:notice] Be it known: a fair maid of the dairy seeketh a husband that can milk. Them that cannot need not apply.
[olde,ch:notice] Item: the friar's mule is strayed again. It is not lost; it knoweth exactly where it is. It is only not here.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] The hunters ask that nobody sing near the river until the fish come back. The fish do not like the new song.
[ch:notice,w:tribal] Whoever borrowed the big pot, the grandmother wants it back, and she does not want it back with anything still in it.
